answer: **No.** This passage is the opening of Fontane's *Effi Briest*, and it is pure static description. It sets out the manor house at Hohen-Cremmen, the garden, the churchyard wall, the pond, the swing, and mother and daughter quietly embroidering an altar carpet. Nothing happens: there is no plot development, character revelation or thematic reversal. Because the excerpt has no turns at all, it cannot have turns that are both surprising and appropriate.
